member_definition.scope: General practice notes for detailing precast concrete work — transport, handling, joints, tolerances. Not member-specific geometry.

key_practice_notes: Precast unit transported after manufacture, before incorporation — tolerances matter when built into part-built/ready-built structures.
Unit often made by third party without site visit/full drawings — clarity of instruction vital.
Special consideration of joints required; sound detailing of joints leads to attractive/serviceable/safe structures.
Casting orientation decision often best left to/discussed with precaster.
Avoid acute re-entrant corners (formwork removal damage) and acute protruding corners (handling breakage, poor aggregate compaction/discoloration).

transport_limits_UK.economic_note: Most frequent load: 20 tonne payload on 32 tonne gross truck; savings if total unit weight per load approaches (without exceeding) 30 tonne, e.g. 2×9.8t vs 1×10.2t.

lifting_and_handling: Permissible support points and packing materials should be noted on drawing.
Lifting strengths for concrete stated on drawing (minimum lifting strength specified for mould-reuse economy).
Unit weight for craneage/transportation stated on drawing.
Reinforcement generally NOT suitable for use as lifting hooks (though some manufacturers do, with care/testing).
Proprietary lifting/fixing inserts used per manufacturer instructions with adequate safety factors; isolate fixings from secondary load effects/structural movements not designed for.
Where a drawing shows part of a unit cast onto another precast unit, clearly state which weights apply to which part.

joints.reference: Design of joints & reinforcement/concrete requirements (binding links, chamfers) covered in IStructE report 'Structural joints in precast concrete', 1978.
joints.in_situ_to_precast_interface: Precast units should have a key joint cast into the mutual face for mechanical anchorage/shear where in-situ concrete is placed adjacent (e.g. infill slab); precast face receiving in-situ concrete should be properly prepared (e.g. scabbled while 'green').

durability_special_case.context: Bridge/car park construction with chloride exposure risk (XD3) — joints between precast units require special corrosion protection attention.
durability_special_case.figure_ref: Figure 8.1 shows moderate/severe/very-severe exposure zones for precast car parks and bridges (splash zone, soffit/beam ends behind sealant, transverse beams/floor slab).

decision_rules.rule: IF a precast unit exceeds 27.4m length, 4.88m height, or falls in the 3.5–5m width band, OR total vehicle+load weight exceeds 44 tonnes THEN special dispensation/notification from the Department for Transport / police is required, per the stated thresholds.
IF a unit is cast onto another precast unit (partial unit) THEN each drawing must clearly state which weights apply and that they are for part units only.

IF in-situ concrete is placed adjacent to precast units (e.g. infill slab) THEN the precast units must have a key joint cast into the mutual face for mechanical anchorage/shear, and the precast face must be properly prepared (e.g. scabbled while green).
IF reinforcement is used as a lifting point THEN this is generally not considered suitable, UNLESS done with proper care, testing, and risk assessment (as some manufacturers do).
IF units are of complex shape or require high-quality single-piece-mould finish THEN they should be discussed with a precaster before finalizing details, and a de-moulding drawing is necessary.
IF chloride exposure risk exists (e.g. bridges/car parks, XD3) THEN joints between precast units require special corrosion-protection attention.

constraints: vehicle_plus_load_weight <= 44 tonne (else Special Types vehicle, STGO tiers)

recovered_information_pass.PR1_surface_finish_tolerance: Designer must make intention clear on surface finish and tolerance; non-standard tolerance areas clearly noted; unnecessarily rigid specifications uneconomic (§8.1, p.160).
recovered_information_pass.PR2_lifting_angles: Lifting position specification must cover permissible support points AND angles of lifting (p.160).
recovered_information_pass.PR3_joint_detail_features: Binding links, chamfers, etc. per IStructE 1978 report (p.161).
recovered_information_pass.PR4_precaster_office_expertise: Detailer needs awareness of moulding, assembly, and handling of cage, typically advised by specialist precaster (p.161).

PR5_severe_exposure_splash_zone.description: Severe-exposure splash zone height on precast car park/bridge beams (Fig 8.1, p.161).
